nations.name: Paiwan
nations.lands: Southern Central Mountain Range across Pingtung and Taitung counties, Taiwan

facts.text: About 102,730 Paiwan people were counted in January 2020, living in the southern mountains of Pingtung and Taitung.
The Ravar branch of the Paiwan is known for outstanding carving and pottery.

nations.name: Wanniyala-Aetto
nations.lands: Eastern Sri Lanka, including the Maduru Oya area

facts.text: In 1983, 51,468 hectares of Wanniyala-Aetto customary land were declared the Maduru Oya National Park.
Their own name, Wanniyala-Aetto, means forest dwellers, and their ancestors lived on the island long before the Sinhalese and the Tamils arrived.

nations.name: Tsou
nations.lands: Alishan Township in Chiayi County, plus Nantou and Kaohsiung, Taiwan

facts.text: The Tsou homeland centres on Alishan Township in Chiayi County, southwest of Yushan in central Taiwan.
The Tsou population was 6,702 in January 2020.

nations.name: Mentawai
nations.lands: The Mentawai Islands, including Siberut, off West Sumatra, Indonesia

facts.text: On Siberut, a UNESCO biosphere reserve since 1981, Mentawai communities use the forest with care, guided by traditional knowledge.

source.title: Siberut Biosphere Reserve, Indonesia
source.publisher: UNESCO Man and the Biosphere Programme

facts.text: Siberut, home to many Mentawai communities, is the largest of the four Mentawai Islands west of Sumatra.

source.title: Siberut Biosphere Reserve, Indonesia
source.publisher: UNESCO Man and the Biosphere Programme

nations.name: Lumad
nations.lands: Mindanao, Philippines

facts.text: Lumad is a shared name for many Indigenous peoples of Mindanao, among them the Manobo, Subanon, Mandaya, Talandig and Teduray.
Lumad advocacy, with allies, helped write two important provisions into the 1987 Philippine Constitution.

nations.name: Khasi
nations.lands: Khasi Hills of Meghalaya, India, and nearby Bangladesh

facts.text: The Khasi Hills Autonomous District Council has a wing that oversees the Elakas, the traditional Khasi states.

source.title: General Administration Department and Elaka Administration

facts.text: Apart from Shillong's municipality and cantonment, all of Meghalaya is governed under the Sixth Schedule, the only northeast state where this is so.

nations.name: Bunun
nations.lands: Both sides of the Central Mountain Range in Nantou, Hualien, Taitung and Kaohsiung, Taiwan

facts.text: The Bunun live higher in the mountains than any other Indigenous people in Taiwan, mostly between 500 and 1,500 metres.
About 59,536 Bunun people were counted in January 2020, with homes in Nantou, Hualien, Taitung and Kaohsiung.

nations.name: Tamang
nations.lands: Hills around the Kathmandu Valley and central Nepal

facts.text: The Tamang are on the Nepal government's official list of Adivasi Janajati, or Indigenous nationalities.

source.title: Adivasi Janajati list
source.publisher: National Foundation for Development of Indigenous Nationalities, Nepal

facts.text: Tamang is the mother tongue of about 4.88 percent of Nepal's population, according to the 2021 census.

nations.name: Akha
nations.lands: Northern Thailand, eastern Myanmar and northern Laos

facts.text: The Akha are one of more than 20 highland Indigenous peoples of northern Thailand.

nations.name: Saisiyat
nations.lands: Hsinchu and Miaoli counties in northwestern Taiwan

facts.text: The Saisiyat live in northwestern Taiwan, in Hsinchu County and Miaoli County on either side of Ngangihaw mountain.
The Saisiyat population was 6,730 in January 2020.

nations.name: Truku
nations.lands: Xiulin, Wanrong and Zhuoxi townships in Hualien County, Taiwan

facts.text: The Truku were officially recognized as one of Taiwan's Indigenous peoples in 2004.
About 32,333 Truku people were counted in January 2020, mostly in Hualien County.

nations.name: Sediq
nations.lands: Mountain areas of Nantou and Hualien in central Taiwan

facts.text: Three subgroups make up the Sediq, each with its own group identity: Seediq Tgdaya, Sediq Toda and Sejiq Truku.
About 10,452 Sediq people were counted in January 2020, mostly in the mountains of Nantou and Hualien.

nations.name: Bhil
nations.lands: Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Rajasthan and Maharashtra, India

facts.text: India's government names the Bhil among the tribal peoples whose movements strengthened the country's freedom struggle.

source.title: Cabinet approves declaration of 15th November as Janjatiya Gaurav Divas
source.publisher: Prime Minister's Office, Government of India

nations.name: Marma
nations.lands: Chittagong Hill Tracts of Bangladesh

facts.text: Together, the Chakma, Marma and Tripura make up about 90 percent of the Indigenous peoples of the Chittagong Hill Tracts.

nations.name: Yakthung
nations.lands: Limbuwan in the eastern hills of Nepal, including Taplejung, Panchthar, Terhathum and Ilam, plus Jhapa, Morang and Sunsari, with communities in Sikkim and Darjeeling, India

facts.text: In Nepal's 2021 census, 84.5 percent of Yakthung people reported Limbu as their mother tongue, a language with its own script, Sirijanga.

source.title: लिम्बु (Limbu)
source.publisher: National Foundation for Development of Indigenous Nationalities, Nepal

facts.text: In 2021 Nepal's Language Commission recommended Limbu, alongside Maithili, as an official language of Province 1 in eastern Nepal.

source.title: Language Commission recommends province-wise official languages before government

nations.name: Tharu
nations.lands: The Terai plains of southern Nepal, and neighbouring India

facts.text: The Tharu are on the Nepal government's official list of Adivasi Janajati, or Indigenous nationalities.

source.title: Adivasi Janajati list
source.publisher: National Foundation for Development of Indigenous Nationalities, Nepal

facts.text: Tharu is the mother tongue of about 5.88 percent of Nepal's population, according to the 2021 census.

nations.name: Kurukh
nations.lands: Jharkhand, Odisha, Chhattisgarh and West Bengal in India, with communities in Assam, Bangladesh and Nepal

facts.text: Odisha counted 358,112 Kurukh (Oraon) people in 2011; many farm and practice crafts such as carpentry, rope making and weaving date palm leaf mats.

source.title: Odisha State Tribal Museum: Oraon
source.publisher: Odisha State Tribal Museum (SCSTRTI, Government of Odisha)

facts.text: Twelve to thirty Kurukh villages join in a Parha council, where members of each village council meet under a Parha chief.

source.title: Oraon
source.publisher: Dr. Ramdayal Munda Tribal Welfare Research Institute, Jharkhand

nations.name: Thao
nations.lands: Ita Thao Village by Sun Moon Lake and Dapinglin, Nantou County, Taiwan

facts.text: Thao people live mainly in Ita Thao Village in Yuchi Township and in Dapinglin, Shuili Township, both in Nantou County. They numbered about 817 in January 2020.
Thao oral history tells of ancestors who followed a white deer to Sun Moon Lake and found a fertile place full of fish.

nations.name: Pinuyumayan
nations.lands: Taitung City and Beinan Township on the Taitung Plain, Taiwan

facts.text: Taitung City and Beinan Township on the Taitung Plain are the heart of Pinuyumayan life today.
About 14,517 Pinuyumayan people were counted in January 2020, and many have moved from eastern Taiwan to cities, where they are active in many fields.

nations.name: Santal
nations.lands: Jharkhand, West Bengal, Odisha and nearby states of India, northwest Bangladesh, and Nepal

facts.text: On 25 December 2025, India's Constitution was released in the Santali language, written in the Ol Chiki script.

source.title: President of India releases the Constitution of India in the Santhali language

facts.text: Santali, the Santal language, is one of the 22 languages listed in the Eighth Schedule of India's Constitution.

source.title: Languages Included in the Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution
source.publisher: Department of Official Language, Ministry of Home Affairs, India

nations.name: Munda
nations.lands: Jharkhand, Odisha, West Bengal, Chhattisgarh and Bihar in India, with communities in Bangladesh

facts.text: Mundari has its own script, known in the community as Mundari Bani; a version reformed in 2008 by Munda community bodies is in the Unicode Standard.

source.title: Chapter 13, South and Central Asia-II (The Unicode Standard, Version 18.0)

facts.text: Munda call their dance durang and their song susun, and both women and men dance at social events and seasonal festivals.

source.title: Munda
source.publisher: Dr. Ramdayal Munda Tribal Welfare Research Institute, Jharkhand

nations.name: Ho
nations.lands: Kolhan region of Jharkhand and northern Odisha, with communities in West Bengal and Bihar, India

facts.text: In Odisha, Ho farmers grow paddy, maize and ragi, tend kitchen gardens, and gather mushrooms, mahua and greens from the forest.

source.title: Odisha State Tribal Museum: Ho
source.publisher: Odisha State Tribal Museum (SCSTRTI, Government of Odisha)

facts.text: The Ho language has its own recently devised alphabet, Warang Citi, which is encoded in the Unicode Standard and used by a yearly and a biweekly publication.

source.title: Chapter 13, South and Central Asia-II (The Unicode Standard, Version 18.0)

nations.name: Kanakanavu
nations.lands: Namaxia District, Kaohsiung City, Taiwan

facts.text: On June 26, 2014, Taiwan's government recognized the Kanakanavu as an independent people, the 16th on the official list.
Some Kanakanavu people understand their name as people living in a forest of Taiwan giant bamboo.

nations.name: Rai
nations.lands: Majh Kirat, also called Khambuwan, in the middle hills of eastern Nepal between the Dudh Koshi and Arun rivers, plus Jhapa, Morang, Sunsari and the Kathmandu Valley

facts.text: The Kirat Rai Yayokkha, founded in 1990, works to unite Nepal's diverse Rai communities and to promote Rai languages, arts and literature.
The Rai are a multilingual people: the Kirat Rai Yayokkha has registered 26 Rai language groups, among them Bantawa, Chamling and Kulung.

source.title: राई (Rai)
source.publisher: National Foundation for Development of Indigenous Nationalities, Nepal

nations.name: Rukai
nations.lands: Southern Central Mountain Range in Kaohsiung, Pingtung and Taitung, Taiwan

facts.text: About 13,465 Rukai people were counted in January 2020, living in Kaohsiung, Pingtung and Taitung.
For the Rukai, the lily stands for purity and courage, and the right to wear lily ornaments sits at the heart of their culture.

nations.name: Gond
nations.lands: Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, Telangana, Odisha and neighboring states of central India

facts.text: Masaram Gondi, a script created in 1918 by Munshi Mangal Singh Masaram of Madhya Pradesh to write the Gondi language, is still used today in handwritten and printed materials.

source.title: Chapter 13, South and Central Asia-II (The Unicode Standard, Version 18.0)

facts.text: Gond painting, mostly made in Patangarh village in Dindori district, gained worldwide recognition after shows in Tokyo and Paris and became a livelihood for many tribal families.

source.title: Gond Art: Details about Gond Tribal Art and Painting of India

nations.name: Dayak
nations.lands: Borneo: Kalimantan (Indonesia), Sabah and Sarawak (Malaysia) and Brunei

facts.text: Dayak is a shared name for many Indigenous peoples of Borneo, by some estimates about 450 ethnolinguistic groups.
Dayak peoples share traditions of longhouse living and customary law known as adat.

nations.name: Wurundjeri Woi Wurrung
nations.lands: Melbourne and surrounding lands, including the Birrarung (Yarra River), Victoria, Australia

facts.text: The Wurundjeri council was set up in 1985 by Wurundjeri descendants and gained Registered Aboriginal Party status for cultural heritage in 2008.

source.title: Recent Past & Present
source.publisher: Wurundjeri Woi Wurrung Cultural Heritage Aboriginal Corporation

facts.text: In 2017 a Yarra River protection bill was the first legislation put before Victoria's parliament with a dual Aboriginal language title: Wilip-gin Birrarung murron, keep the Birrarung alive.

source.title: Recent Past & Present
source.publisher: Wurundjeri Woi Wurrung Cultural Heritage Aboriginal Corporation

nations.name: iTaukei
nations.lands: Fiji

facts.text: The iTaukei Land Trust Board, set up in 1940, manages iTaukei land for its owners, whether a yavusa, mataqali or tokatoka.
The iTaukei Affairs Board, set up in 1944 as the Fijian Affairs Board, is the main advisory and coordinating body for iTaukei affairs, supporting village, tikina and provincial leaders.

nations.name: Kosraeans
nations.lands: Kosrae, an island state in the east of the Federated States of Micronesia, with the municipalities of Lelu, Malem, Tafunsak and Utwe

facts.text: Kosrae State has its own constitutional government, with a legislature elected by voters in the districts of Lelu, Malem, Tafunsak and Utwe.

source.title: Kosrae
source.publisher: Legal Information System of the Federated States of Micronesia

facts.text: In 2017 Kosraean elders proposed protecting Kosrae's mountain range, seen as the figure Mahkontowe, now the Mahkontowe Conservation Area under Kosrae State law.

nations.name: Moriori
nations.lands: Rēkohu and Rangihaute (the Chatham and Pitt Islands), Aotearoa New Zealand

facts.text: Moriori are the Indigenous people of Rēkohu and Rangihaute, the Chatham Islands, and are represented by the Hokotehi Moriori Trust.
The Hokotehi Moriori Trust takes part in key parts of the Rēkohu economy, such as fishing, farming and tourism.

nations.name: Gadigal
nations.lands: The southern side of Sydney Harbour (Port Jackson), from South Head to around Petersham, in Sydney, New South Wales, Australia

facts.text: Descendants of the Eora still live in Sydney today and proudly use the name Eora.
The City of Sydney formally acknowledges the Gadigal of the Eora Nation as the traditional custodians of the place now called Sydney.

nations.name: Larrakia
nations.lands: The Darwin region, from Cox Peninsula in the west to Gunn Point in the north, Northern Territory, Australia

facts.text: Larrakia Nation Aboriginal Corporation, set up in 1997, runs about 40 programs in Darwin, including the Larrakia Land and Sea Rangers.
Larrakia are the traditional owners of the Darwin region, with country reaching from Cox Peninsula in the west up to Gunn Point in the north.

nations.name: Marshallese
nations.lands: the atolls and islands of the Republic of the Marshall Islands, including Majuro

facts.text: Waan Aelõñ in Majel, Canoes of the Marshall Islands, is a Majuro program that trains young Marshallese women and men in skills for a sustainable future.

source.title: Canoes of the Marshall Islands, Waan Aelõñ in Majel

facts.text: A Marshallese stick chart maps how ocean swells bend around islands, with cowrie shells for the islands, and is studied before a voyage rather than used at sea.

source.title: Stick Navigation Chart
source.publisher: Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History

nations.name: Kaurna
nations.lands: The Adelaide Plains of South Australia, from around Crystal Brook in the north, bounded by the Mount Lofty Ranges to the east, Australia

facts.text: In March 2018 Kaurna people were recognised as native title holders around Adelaide, the first positive native title determination over a capital city area.

source.title: Native Title Recognition For Kaurna People Over Adelaide Area

facts.text: Requests for Kaurna names and translations all go through Kaurna Warra Karrpanthi, an Aboriginal corporation.

source.title: Aboriginal people of South Australia: Kaurna

nations.name: Torres Strait Islanders
nations.lands: the islands of the Torres Strait between Cape York and Papua New Guinea, in Queensland, Australia, and the Northern Peninsula Area

facts.text: The Torres Strait Regional Authority, an Australian Government body set up on 1 July 1994, counts recognising and maintaining Torres Strait Islander Ailan Kastom among its functions.
Kala Lagaw Ya is the traditional language of the western and central Torres Strait islands, and Meriam Mir is the language of the eastern islands.

nations.name: Noongar
nations.lands: The south-west of Western Australia, including the Perth region, Australia

facts.text: Western Australia's settlement recognises the Noongar people as the traditional owners of the South-West, with about A$1.3 billion in land and other benefits.

source.title: All six South West Native Title Settlement Agreements registered

facts.text: The South West Native Title Settlement covers about 200,000 square kilometres and affects an estimated 40,000 Noongar people.

source.title: South West Aboriginal Land and Sea Council
source.publisher: South West Aboriginal Land and Sea Council

nations.name: Yolŋu
nations.lands: North-east Arnhem Land, including the Gove Peninsula, Northern Territory, Australia

facts.text: Yolŋu elders founded Dhimurru Aboriginal Corporation to manage their land on the Gove Peninsula and the visitors who come to it.

source.title: Only Yolŋu make decisions for this land
source.publisher: Office of the Registrar of Indigenous Corporations (Australian Government)

facts.text: The name Dhimurru means east wind, the wind that carries the monsoon rains and brings new life to the land.

source.title: Only Yolŋu make decisions for this land
source.publisher: Office of the Registrar of Indigenous Corporations (Australian Government)

nations.name: Waikato-Tainui
nations.lands: The Waikato region of the North Island, Aotearoa New Zealand

facts.text: Waikato-Tainui describes itself as a growing tribe of over 90,000 people, voyagers and pioneers like their ancestors.

source.title: Ko Waikato te iwi, ko Tainui te waka

facts.text: Waikato-Tainui celebrate their identity as people of the Tainui waka and as protectors of the Kiingitanga movement.

source.title: Ko Waikato te iwi, ko Tainui te waka

nations.name: Niueans
nations.lands: the island of Niue in the South Pacific, with villages such as Alofi, Mutalau and Toi

facts.text: Fale Tāoga Niue, home of the Niue National Museum, opened on 19 October 2018, the anniversary of the Niue Constitution Celebrations.
Niue's Vagahau Niue Act 2012 recognises Vagahau Niue as the official language of Niue and created the Niue Language Commission to protect it.

source.title: Vagahau Niue Act 2012
source.publisher: Université Laval, CEFAN: L'aménagement linguistique dans le monde

nations.name: Samoans
nations.lands: the Independent State of Samoa, on Upolu, Savai'i and nearby islands

facts.text: Women and master weavers have formed fine mat committees in their villages, and more young women, and some men, now weave the 'ie Samoa.

source.title: 'Ie Samoa, fine mat and its cultural value

facts.text: Samoa's 2021 census counted 16,082 people aged 21 and over who hold a matai, or chiefly, title, including 1,444 women.

source.title: Samoa Population and Housing Census 2021 Fact Sheet (Final Results, October 2022)

nations.name: Chuukese
nations.lands: Chuuk State in the Federated States of Micronesia, on the high islands of Chuuk Lagoon such as Weno, Tonoas, Uman and Fefan, and outlying atolls

facts.text: Chuuk's state constitution says existing Chuukese custom and tradition shall be respected, and lets traditional leaders hold formal roles in government.

source.title: Chuuk State Constitution, Article IV
source.publisher: Legal Information System of the Federated States of Micronesia

facts.text: Chuuk's constitution recognizes traditional rights over all reefs, tidelands and other submerged lands, including the water above them.

source.title: Chuuk State Constitution, Article IV
source.publisher: Legal Information System of the Federated States of Micronesia

nations.name: Palauans
nations.lands: the Republic of Palau in the western Pacific, with 16 states on Babeldaob, Koror and other islands

facts.text: Palauans still use the Rock Islands Southern Lagoon, a World Heritage site since 2012, for cultural purposes under a traditional governance system.
Palau's Council of Chiefs, made up of the highest traditional chiefs from each state, advises the President on traditional laws and customs.

nations.name: Gunantuna
nations.lands: the Gazelle Peninsula of New Britain Island, East New Britain Province, Papua New Guinea

facts.text: Diwarra pays for everyday things such as store goods and school fees, and sharing it out expresses ties between clans and individuals.

source.title: Gunantuna (Tolai people)
source.publisher: Queensland Art Gallery | Gallery of Modern Art

facts.text: In 2016 a Queensland gallery commissioned A Bit na Ta, a collaborative work made with the wider Tolai community whose music carries the rhythms of Tolai life from 1875 to 1975.

source.title: Art from Papua New Guinea Celebrated in Major QAG Exhibition
source.publisher: Queensland Art Gallery | Gallery of Modern Art

nations.name: Whanganui Iwi
nations.lands: The Whanganui River, from the mountains to the sea, North Island, Aotearoa New Zealand

facts.text: Ngā Tāngata Tiaki o Whanganui, the iwi river trust, was established in August 2014 with the signing of Ruruku Whakatupua.

source.title: Home | Ngā Tāngata Tiaki o Whanganui

facts.text: Since 2017, New Zealand law has recognised the Whanganui River, Te Awa Tupua, as a legal person, with a guardian office that acts as its human face.

source.title: The Whanganui River (Te Awa Tupua)
source.publisher: OsloMet (Oslo Metropolitan University), River Rights project

nations.name: Ngāi Tahu
nations.lands: Te Waipounamu (the South Island), Aotearoa New Zealand

facts.text: There are 18 Papatipu Rūnanga, local Ngāi Tahu councils, spread throughout Te Waipounamu, the South Island.

source.title: Ngāi Tahu | Te Rūnanga o Ngāi Tahu

facts.text: Ngāi Tahu means people of Tahu, and whakapapa, the ancestral link, binds all Ngāi Tahu whānau.

source.title: Ngāi Tahu | Te Rūnanga o Ngāi Tahu

nations.name: Nauruans
nations.lands: the island of Nauru, officially styled Naoero, in the central Pacific

facts.text: Nauru's government now presents the country as the Republic of Naoero on its official website.

source.title: The Government of the Republic of Naoero
source.publisher: Government of the Republic of Nauru

facts.text: In Nauru's 2021 census, 69 percent of residents aged 5 and over spoke only Nauruan at home, and another 25.3 percent spoke it with another language.

source.title: Nauru 2021 Population and Housing Census: Analytical Report

nations.name: Ngāti Whātua Ōrākei
nations.lands: Central Tāmaki Makaurau (Auckland), Aotearoa New Zealand

facts.text: Ngāti Whātua Ōrākei's shared affairs are looked after by their Trust and two subsidiaries: Whai Māia, the social arm, and Whai Rawa, the commercial arm.
Ngāti Whātua Ōrākei are the tangata whenua, the people of the land, of Te Kahu Tōpuni o Tuperiri in central Tāmaki Makaurau (Auckland).

nations.name: Refaluwasch
nations.lands: Saipan and other islands of the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands, a United States commonwealth in the western Pacific

facts.text: In December 2020 the Matawal Wóól Display Hall opened with photos and crafts made by students of the Tepengi Kkosch Refaluwasch culture program.

source.title: Carolinian Affairs Office 2021 Citizen Centric Report

facts.text: The Carolinian Affairs Office, created by the CNMI Constitution, advises the governor and works to protect and preserve the culture and traditions of Indigenous Carolinians.

source.title: Carolinian Affairs Office 2020 Citizen Centric Report

nations.name: Pohnpeians
nations.lands: Pohnpei State in the Federated States of Micronesia, on Pohnpei island and its outlying atolls

facts.text: Nan Madol, a World Heritage site since 2016, is traditionally owned and managed under the Nahnmwarki system, a chiefly institution that continues in Pohnpei today.

source.title: Nan Madol: Ceremonial Centre of Eastern Micronesia

facts.text: Pohnpei State's constitution protects the customs and traditions of Pohnpei's traditional kingdoms alongside its elected government.

source.title: Pohnpei
source.publisher: Legal Information System of the Federated States of Micronesia

nations.name: Delaware Nation
nations.lands: Anadarko, Oklahoma, United States; Lenape homelands on the Eastern Seaboard

facts.text: Delaware Nation is a federally recognized tribe based in Anadarko, Oklahoma.
In December 2022 Delaware Nation re-established its Tribal Historic Preservation Office to identify and protect cultural resources in Lenape homelands.

source.title: Delaware Nation Re-Established THPO Status with the National Park Services and US Department of Interior

nations.name: Wampanoag Tribe of Gay Head (Aquinnah)
nations.lands: Aquinnah, on the western end of Martha's Vineyard (Noepe), Massachusetts, United States

facts.text: The Aquinnah Wampanoag care for 477 acres of their ancestral lands on Martha's Vineyard.
In 1998 the town of Gay Head returned to its former Wampanoag name, Aquinnah.

nations.name: Tuscarora Nation
nations.lands: Tuscarora Nation territory near Lewiston, western New York, United States; earlier homelands in what is now North Carolina

facts.text: The Tuscarora Language Program works with one clear mission: to revive a community of Tuscarora speakers.
The Tuscarora Environment Program works as part of the Haudenosaunee Environmental Task Force, established in 1992 by the Grand Council.

nations.name: Mashpee Wampanoag Tribe
nations.lands: Mashpee on Cape Cod, Massachusetts, United States; Wampanoag homelands across present-day Massachusetts and eastern Rhode Island

facts.text: The Mashpee Wampanoag were re-acknowledged as a federally recognized tribe in 2007.

source.title: Mashpee Wampanoag Tribe | People of the First Light

facts.text: Children at Mukayuhsak Weekuw, the Mashpee Wampanoag language nest, could be the first in centuries to grow up proficient in Wôpanâak.

nations.name: Chickahominy Indian Tribe
nations.lands: the Chickahominy River area and Chickahominy Ridge in Virginia, as described in the Tribe's history

facts.text: The Chickahominy Indian Tribe's history describes permanent villages along the Virginia river that still bears its name.
The Tribe dates the establishment of Samaria Indian Baptist Church, a community institution, to 1901.

nations.name: United Keetoowah Band of Cherokee Indians in Oklahoma
nations.lands: Tahlequah, Oklahoma, United States

facts.text: The UKB Tribal Council is made up of four officers and nine district representatives, governing from Tahlequah, Oklahoma.

source.title: United Keetoowah Band | Home | Tahlequah, OK
source.publisher: United Keetoowah Band of Cherokee Indians in Oklahoma

facts.text: The United Keetoowah Band numbers more than 14,000 tribal members today.

source.title: About Us | United Keetoowah Band | Tahlequah
source.publisher: United Keetoowah Band of Cherokee Indians in Oklahoma

pronounce.publisher: United Keetoowah Band of Cherokee Indians in Oklahoma, on its own site

nations.name: Monacan Indian Nation
nations.lands: Bear Mountain in Amherst County, Virginia; the Nation describes ancestral homelands extending through Virginia and parts of West Virginia and North Carolina

facts.text: The Nation says its Priority Climate Action Plan includes a greenhouse gas inventory to guide conservation and emissions-reduction work.
The Nation describes its citizens as descendants of Virginia and North Carolina Eastern Siouan cultural and linguistic groups.

nations.name: Nansemond Indian Nation
nations.lands: the Nansemond River area of southeastern Virginia; the Nation describes traditional settlements extending into northeastern North Carolina

facts.text: The Nation's published Environmental Program describes oyster restoration, invasive plant removal and native plant restoration.
The Nation's history dates formal organization with elected officers to 1984.

nations.name: Muscogee Nation
nations.lands: Okmulgee and the Muscogee reservation in eastern Oklahoma, United States; original homelands in present-day Georgia and Alabama

facts.text: Seated in Okmulgee, Oklahoma, the Muscogee (Creek) Nation is self-governed and organized by its Constitution into three branches of government.
The Mvskoke Language Program offers classes and learning resources so Mvskoke people can keep their language, culture and sovereignty strong.

nations.name: Chickahominy Indian Tribe - Eastern Division
nations.lands: New Kent County, Virginia; the Tribe describes roots in Virginia before English colonization

facts.text: In its food-sovereignty account, CIT-ED says a 2022 EPA grant supported a community compost and gardening program.
The Tribe's timeline records a certificate of incorporation for the Chickahominy Indians Eastern Division in 1925.

nations.name: Narragansett Indian Tribe
nations.lands: Rhode Island, United States

facts.text: The Narragansett Indian Tribe received federal recognition and acknowledgement on April 11, 1983.
A land claim brought by the Tribe ended in a 1978 out-of-court settlement of about 1,800 acres.

nations.name: Sappony
nations.lands: the High Plains Indian Settlement along the North Carolina-Virginia boundary, including Person County, North Carolina, and Halifax County, Virginia, as described by Sappony

facts.text: Sappony describes committees addressing education, cultural preservation and economic development.
Sappony's governance page describes a council with one elected representative from each of the settlement's seven families.

nations.name: The Chickasaw Nation
nations.lands: Thirteen counties in south-central Oklahoma, United States; original homelands in present-day Mississippi, Alabama and Tennessee

facts.text: The Chickasaw Nation's three-department government was reestablished with the ratification of its 1983 Constitution.
The Chickasaw language revitalization program began in 2007, and its master-apprentice program pairs learners with fluent Chickasaw speakers.

nations.name: Catawba Nation
nations.lands: York County, South Carolina, near Rock Hill, with a service area that includes North Carolina, United States

facts.text: After a 20-year effort, a land claim settlement on November 20, 1993 brought the Catawba Indian Nation federal recognition.
The Catawba Nation has over 3,300 enrolled citizens and continues to grow.

nations.name: Haliwa-Saponi Indian Tribe
nations.lands: the Meadows area at present-day Hollister, North Carolina; the Tribe locates its government there without defining territorial boundaries in this source

facts.text: The Tribe describes Red Earth as a program for all ages to learn about Haliwa-Saponi history and cultural practices.

source.title: Cultural Classes - Haliwa Saponi Tribe Resources

facts.text: The Tribal School's stated mission combines academics, technology and community involvement with American Indian culture.

source.title: Haliwa Saponi Tribal School: Quality Education - Haliwa Saponi Tribe Resources

nations.name: Waccamaw Siouan Tribe
nations.lands: Bladen and Columbus Counties in southeastern North Carolina, near Green Swamp

facts.text: Its government page describes a Tribal Council elected by the membership and an Elders Review Committee.
The Tribe's introduction places its communities mainly in Bladen and Columbus Counties, North Carolina, near Green Swamp.

nations.name: Onondaga Nation
nations.lands: Onondaga Nation territory south of Syracuse, central New York, United States

facts.text: In the Haudenosaunee Grand Council, the Onondaga Fire Keepers present an issue, and debate goes on until they can announce that all are of One Mind, a decision by consensus.
The Onondaga Nation is still governed by its traditional government, with fourteen Chiefs and their Clan Mothers serving as caretakers of the land.

nations.name: Cayuga Nation
nations.lands: Around Cayuga Lake in the Finger Lakes region of New York, United States

facts.text: After more than 200 years away, Cayuga Nation citizens once again live on their ancestral homeland in New York's Finger Lakes region.
Every citizen of the Cayuga Nation belongs to one of the Nation's five clans.

nations.name: Pamunkey Indian Tribe
nations.lands: Pamunkey Reservation on the Pamunkey River, King William County, Virginia, United States

facts.text: The U.S. Department of the Interior acknowledged the Pamunkey Indian Tribe as federally recognized, effective January 28, 2016.
The Pamunkey reservation sits on the northern bank of the Pamunkey River in King William County, Virginia.

nations.name: Cherokee Tribe of Northeast Alabama
nations.lands: Northeast Alabama; its own introduction traces its roots to the lower Cherokee towns.

facts.text: Its government page describes a Tribal Council with one representative for each district.
Its Learning Tools page presents a syllabary song and a public word-learning list.

nations.name: Upper Mattaponi Tribe
nations.lands: King William County, Virginia; the Tribe describes its community base as within the traditional lands of Tsenacomacah

facts.text: The Tribe's school history says King William County returned Sharon Indian School to the Tribe in 1987.

source.title: Sharon Indian School Foundation - Upper Mattaponi Tribe

facts.text: The Tribe's history says the Adamstown band became officially known as the Upper Mattaponi Tribe in 1921.

nations.name: Northern Cheyenne Tribe
nations.lands: Northern Cheyenne Reservation, southeastern Montana, United States; headquarters in Lame Deer

facts.text: Lame Deer, Montana, is home to the Northern Cheyenne tribal government headquarters, and the Tribal Council is elected by district.

source.title: Northern Cheyenne Tribe
source.publisher: Montana Governor's Office of Indian Affairs

facts.text: About 99 percent of the Northern Cheyenne Reservation, roughly 444,000 acres in southeastern Montana, is owned by the tribe.

source.title: Northern Cheyenne Tribe
source.publisher: Montana Governor's Office of Indian Affairs

nations.name: Comanche Nation
nations.lands: Southwest Oklahoma, United States; headquarters north of Lawton

facts.text: The Comanche Nation's main governing body is its Tribal Council, made up of every enrolled member over age 18.
The Comanche Nation language program works to revitalize and reclaim the Comanche language, including through online learning.

pronounce.text: Nʉmʉnʉʉ, the Comanche name for the people: NUH-MUH-NUH
pronounce.publisher: Comanche Nation, on its own site

nations.name: Apsáalooke Nation
nations.lands: Crow Indian Reservation, south-central Montana, United States; headquarters at Crow Agency

facts.text: The Apsáalooke Nation's government has three branches: executive, legislative and judicial.

source.title: Official Site of the Crow Tribe Executive Branch - Home

facts.text: Montana's state tribal directory reports that most Apsáalooke people speak Crow as their first language.

source.title: Crow Nation
source.publisher: Montana Governor's Office of Indian Affairs

nations.name: Spirit Lake Nation
nations.lands: Northeastern North Dakota, mainly Benson County, United States; headquarters at Fort Totten

facts.text: Cankdeska Cikana Community College, the tribal college at Spirit Lake, offers 12 associate degree and certificate programs.

source.title: Spirit Lake Nation | Indian Affairs Commission, North Dakota

facts.text: At Spirit Lake both English and the Dakota language are spoken, specifically the Eastern Dakota dialect.

source.title: Spirit Lake Nation | Indian Affairs Commission, North Dakota

nations.name: Ponca Tribe of Nebraska
nations.lands: Fifteen-county service area across Nebraska, Iowa and South Dakota, United States

facts.text: The tribe serves its people across a fifteen-county service area in Nebraska, Iowa and South Dakota, set up by the Ponca Restoration Act.
The Ponca Restoration Act, signed by President George H. W. Bush, restored federal recognition to the Ponca Tribe of Nebraska.

nations.name: Cheyenne River Sioux Tribe
nations.lands: Cheyenne River Reservation, central South Dakota, United States; headquarters in Eagle Butte

facts.text: The tribe is governed by a Chairman, Vice-Chairman, Secretary, Treasurer and fifteen council members, with headquarters in Eagle Butte.

source.title: Cheyenne River Agency | Indian Affairs
source.publisher: U.S. Department of the Interior, Bureau of Indian Affairs

facts.text: The Cheyenne River Reservation holds about 1.45 million trust acres in Ziebach and Dewey counties in central South Dakota.

source.title: Cheyenne River Agency | Indian Affairs
source.publisher: U.S. Department of the Interior, Bureau of Indian Affairs

nations.name: Iowa Tribe of Kansas and Nebraska
nations.lands: Reservation along the Kansas and Nebraska border, United States

facts.text: The tribe is governed by two bodies, a General Council and an Executive Committee.

source.title: Welcome to the Iowa Tribe of Kansas and Nebraska
source.publisher: Iowa Tribe of Kansas and Nebraska

facts.text: The reservation of the Iowa Tribe of Kansas and Nebraska straddles the eastern border between the two states, and tribal headquarters is on it.

source.title: Welcome to the Iowa Tribe of Kansas and Nebraska
source.publisher: Iowa Tribe of Kansas and Nebraska

nations.name: Mandan, Hidatsa, and Arikara Nation
nations.lands: Fort Berthold Indian Reservation, central North Dakota, United States

facts.text: The MHA Nation is governed by a Chairman and six Segment Representatives, one each for White Shield, Parshall, New Town, Four Bears, Mandaree and Twin Buttes.

source.title: MHA Nation | Mandan, Hidatsa, and Arikara Nation

facts.text: The nation greets visitors in all three of its languages. In Mandan, Ráátinitak shí’sh means it is good that you all arrived.

source.title: MHA Nation | Mandan, Hidatsa, and Arikara Nation

nations.name: Northern Arapaho Tribe
nations.lands: Wind River Reservation, Wyoming, United States, shared with the Eastern Shoshone

facts.text: The Northern Arapaho and the Eastern Shoshone share a 2.2 million acre reservation in Wyoming, between the Wind River Range and the Owl Creek Mountains.
The Arapaho Flag was created in 1936 to honor and remember Arapaho war veterans.

nations.name: Sac and Fox Nation
nations.lands: Central Oklahoma, United States; headquarters in Stroud

facts.text: The Sac and Fox Nation supports learning Sauk through an interactive language website and a concise Sauk dictionary.
The Sac and Fox Nation was the first tribe to take on self-governance within the Indian Health Service.

nations.name: Forest County Potawatomi
nations.lands: Forest County, northern Wisconsin, United States

facts.text: The Forest County Potawatomi Language and Culture Department works to keep the Bodwéwadmi language and traditions alive, with classes during the school year.
The Forest County Potawatomi Cultural Center, Library and Museum provides an important link to the community's past.

nations.name: Red Lake Nation
also: Red Lake Band of Chippewa Indians
nations.lands: Red Lake Reservation, northern Minnesota, United States

facts.text: The Red Lake tribal government holds full sovereignty over its reservation, subject only to the federal government.

source.title: Red Lake Nation - Home of the Red Lake Band of Chippewa Indians

facts.text: English is a second language for many Red Lake members who are middle-aged and older, including some on the Tribal Council, and many others speak or understand Ojibwe.

nations.name: Kiowa Tribe
nations.lands: Southwestern Oklahoma, United States

facts.text: The Kiowa Tribe commits to protecting its sovereignty and to preserving and advocating for Kiowa culture and language.

source.title: Kiowa Tribe - Tribe, Native American, Native, Tribe

facts.text: The Kiowa Language Department runs a credentialed teacher training program to prepare new Kiowa language teachers.

pronounce.text: Gáuigú, as in Gáuigú bà dàu, We are Kiowa: Gkawy-goo
pronounce.publisher: Kiowa Tribe, on its own site

nations.name: Blackfeet Nation
nations.lands: Blackfeet Reservation, northwestern Montana, bordering Canada and Glacier National Park, United States

facts.text: The Blackfeet Reservation covers about one and a half million acres, bordered by Canada to the north and Glacier National Park to the west.

source.title: Blackfeet Nation
source.publisher: Montana Governor's Office of Indian Affairs

facts.text: The Blackfeet Nation describes itself as a nation of 17,321 members.

nations.name: Little Traverse Bay Bands of Odawa Indians
nations.lands: Northern Lower Peninsula of Michigan, United States

facts.text: The tribe is governed by a nine-member Tribal Council whose members serve staggered terms.

source.title: Home - LTBB Official Website
source.publisher: Little Traverse Bay Bands of Odawa Indians

facts.text: The tribe's mission celebrates that its people still have and speak their own language, Anishinaabemowin.

source.title: Home - LTBB Official Website
source.publisher: Little Traverse Bay Bands of Odawa Indians

nations.name: Menominee Indian Tribe of Wisconsin
nations.lands: Menominee Reservation, northeastern Wisconsin, United States

facts.text: The Menominee Tribal Legislature has nine members.
The Menominee Reservation covers about 235,524 acres in Wisconsin and holds the largest single tract of virgin timberland in the state.

nations.name: Otoe-Missouria Tribe
nations.lands: Red Rock, Oklahoma; historical homelands include Nebraska and the lower Missouri River valley

facts.text: The Tribe's government page describes a seven-member Tribal Council elected by qualified Tribal voters using a secret ballot.
The Tribe's preservation page dates National Park Service recognition of its Tribal Historic Preservation Office to spring 2016.

nations.name: Fort Peck Assiniboine and Sioux Tribes
nations.lands: Fort Peck Reservation, northeastern Montana, United States; headquarters in Poplar

facts.text: Members of the Fort Peck Tribal Executive Board, except the secretary-accountant, are elected at-large every two years.

source.title: Fort Peck Assiniboine and Sioux Tribes
source.publisher: Montana Governor's Office of Indian Affairs

facts.text: The Fort Peck Reservation in northeastern Montana includes more than two million acres of land.

source.title: Fort Peck Assiniboine and Sioux Tribes
source.publisher: Montana Governor's Office of Indian Affairs

nations.name: Prairie Band Potawatomi Nation
nations.lands: Reservation near Mayetta, northeastern Kansas, United States

facts.text: The Nation has offered Potawatomi language classes since 2007 as part of its work to revitalize the language and culture.

source.title: Prairie Band Potawatomi Language Revitalization Efforts

facts.text: The Prairie Band Potawatomi Nation says its Kansas reservation is unchanged from what the Treaty of 1846 established.

source.title: Prairie Band Potawatomi Tribal History: Origins, Separation, and Stewardship

nations.name: Ho-Chunk Nation
nations.lands: Wisconsin, United States, on lands in many places rather than one reservation; traditional lands also reach Minnesota, Iowa, Missouri and Illinois

facts.text: The Ho-Chunk Nation has four branches of government, with a legislature of 13 members elected from four districts.
Alongside its constitutional government, the Ho-Chunk Nation keeps a traditional system of leadership based on chiefs and clans.

nations.name: Sicangu Lakota Oyate
nations.lands: Rosebud Reservation, South Dakota, United States

facts.text: The tribe's history page says the Lakota number about 70,000 today, and that about a third of them still speak their ancestral language.
The Rosebud Reservation takes in 20 communities, and the tribal headquarters is in the community of Rosebud, South Dakota.

nations.name: Benet
nations.lands: the slopes of Mount Elgon in eastern Uganda, in Kween, Kapchorwa and Bukwo districts

facts.text: In May 2023 Uganda's Office of the Prime Minister directed the wildlife authority (UWA) to stop evictions of Benet communities.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2024, Uganda chapter (IWGIA yearbook PDF)
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

facts.text: In 2005 Uganda's High Court recognized the Benet as the historical, indigenous inhabitants of Mount Elgon, a landmark land-rights ruling.

source.title: Momentous Ruling Recognizes Land Rights of Indigenous Community

nations.name: Bagyeli
nations.lands: the forests of southern Cameroon, around Akom II, Bipindi, Kribi and Lolodorf

facts.text: In late 2018 Bagyeli communities filed three Community Forest applications with Cameroon's forestry ministry, after mapping their own forest use.

source.title: Secure land tenure: The legal battles of the Bagyeli

facts.text: Bagyeli and Bakola communities live across about 12,000 km2 of southern Cameroon, especially around Akom II, Bipindi, Kribi and Lolodorf.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2024, Cameroon chapter (IWGIA yearbook PDF)
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

nations.name: Ovahimba
nations.lands: Kunene Region of north-western Namibia and south-western Angola

facts.text: Ovahimba speak a Herero language and keep semi-nomadic herding homelands that reach from north-western Namibia into south-western Angola.
Ovahimba are mainly herders whose homes lie in the dry mountains and plains of north-west Namibia's Kunene Region.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2026: Namibia
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

nations.name: Oromo
nations.lands: Oromia and other regions of Ethiopia, and northern Kenya

facts.text: Knowledge of the Gada system is passed on to Oromo children today, at home and at school.

source.title: Gada system, an indigenous democratic socio-political system of the Oromo

facts.text: UNESCO lists the Gada system as an indigenous democratic socio-political system of the Oromo, inscribed on its heritage list in 2016.

source.title: Gada system, an indigenous democratic socio-political system of the Oromo

nations.name: Ishelhiyen
nations.lands: the Souss valley, the Anti-Atlas and the western High Atlas of south-western Morocco

facts.text: In the Souss-Massa region, 63.2% of residents use Tachelhit, the language of the Ishelhin, according to Morocco's 2024 census.

source.title: RGPH 2024: Caractéristiques démographiques et socioéconomiques de la population, Région Souss-Massa
source.publisher: Haut-Commissariat au Plan (HCP), Direction Régionale de Souss Massa

facts.text: Tachelhit, the language of the Ishelhin of southern Morocco, is one of three Amazigh languages taught at Inalco in Paris.

source.title: Kabyle (Berber)
source.publisher: Inalco (Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales)

nations.name: Hadzabe
nations.lands: the hills and valleys around Lake Eyasi in northern Tanzania

facts.text: Hadzabe communities are calling for community-led tourism that ensures transparency, dignity and a fair share of the benefits.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2026: Tanzania
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

facts.text: Hadza people speak Hadzane, a language isolate, which means it is not related to any other known language.

nations.name: Nama
nations.lands: southern Namibia and the Richtersveld and Namaqualand areas of South Africa's Northern Cape, with smaller communities in Botswana

facts.text: In 2003 South Africa's Constitutional Court recognized the Richtersveld Nama community's communal Indigenous right to its land and the resources in it.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2026: South Africa
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

facts.text: In South Africa's Richtersveld, Nama families still build portable rush-mat houses called haru oms and move herds between seasonal grazing grounds.

nations.name: Mbororo
nations.lands: Cameroon, Chad, Nigeria, the Central African Republic and Niger, often along borderland grazing routes

facts.text: Hindou Oumarou Ibrahim, a Mbororo woman from Chad who founded the group AFPAT, chaired the UN Permanent Forum on Indigenous Issues for its 2024 session.

source.title: Previous Chairpersons of the Permanent Forum
source.publisher: United Nations, Department of Economic and Social Affairs (UNPFII)

facts.text: Mbororo pastoralists in Cameroon are estimated at over one million people, living mainly near the borders with Nigeria, Chad and the Central African Republic.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2026: Cameroon
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

nations.name: Naro
nations.lands: Ghanzi District in western Botswana, and eastern Namibia

facts.text: In 2025 Botswana's government started radio programs in a number of Indigenous languages, Naro among them.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2026: Botswana
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

facts.text: Botswana chose Naro, the main San language of Ghanzi District, as one of the mother-tongue languages for primary school teaching from 2022.

source.title: Forty years of fighting for literacy The case of Naro Bible translators

nations.name: Tshwa
nations.lands: Tsholotsho and Bulilimamangwe districts of western Zimbabwe

facts.text: Zimbabwe's 2013 Constitution lists Koisan among its 16 languages, and in 2023 the Tsoro-o-tso San Development Trust worked on the Tjwao language.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2024, Zimbabwe chapter (IWGIA yearbook PDF)
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

facts.text: About 3,207 Tshwa live in Zimbabwe, where they self-identify as an Indigenous people, mostly in the western districts.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2024, Zimbabwe chapter (IWGIA yearbook PDF)
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

nations.name: Batwa
nations.lands: south-western Uganda, Rwanda, Burundi and the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo

facts.text: In Burundi, Batwa have been represented in the country's main decision-making bodies since 2005.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2023: Burundi
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

facts.text: In 2021 Uganda's Constitutional Court found that Batwa were evicted from ancestral lands without consent and sent the question of compensation to a lower court.

source.title: MRG welcomes Uganda court verdict on Batwa compensation

nations.name: Samburu
nations.lands: Samburu County and nearby rangelands of north-central Kenya

facts.text: All of Reteti's elephant keepers come from the Samburu community and are formally trained to care for, rehabilitate and release elephant calves.

source.title: Home | Reteti Elephant Sanctuary in Kenya

facts.text: With support from the Samburu Women's Trust, Samburu women are exercising land rights: 20 women and three women's groups own land in one home area.

source.title: Empowering women means taking a stand for environmental rights

nations.name: Khoikhoi
nations.lands: South Africa, especially the Western, Northern and Eastern Cape, including Nama, Griqua and Korana communities

facts.text: Rooibos benefit money now helps fund local schools, water pumps, student fees and an organic rooibos nursery in Cederberg communities such as Wupperthal.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2026: South Africa
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

facts.text: The Khoisan revival is an ongoing cultural, social and academic movement in South Africa, centred on identity and reclaiming history.

source.title: Kora: A Lost Khoisan Language of the early Cape and the Gariep, Introduction (Menán du Plessis)

nations.name: ǂKhomani
nations.lands: the southern Kalahari in South Africa's Northern Cape, including the Kalahari Gemsbok National Park near the borders with Botswana and Namibia

facts.text: ǂKhomani people have won back cultural rights in South Africa's Kalahari Gemsbok National Park, such as using its resources and hunting in traditional ways across much of it.
The ǂKhomani are actively reclaiming their knowledge and traditions. Their Kalahari homeland became a UNESCO World Heritage cultural landscape in 2017.

nations.name: Ju|'hoansi
nations.lands: Nyae Nyae and the Tsumkwe area of north-eastern Namibia, and neighbouring north-western Botswana

facts.text: When Ju|'hoansi formed their farmers' cooperative, they began with open consensus meetings, then elected two representatives per community, at least one of them a woman.

source.title: Controlling Their Destiny: Ju|'hoansi of Nyae Nyae

facts.text: Ju|'hoansi is the one San language Namibia has approved for teaching in schools, but a 2025 review of 14 schools found it is seldom used in class.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2026: Namibia
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

nations.name: Mbuti
nations.lands: the Ituri forest of north-eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo

facts.text: A 2022 national law in the DR Congo, in force since February 2023, recognizes the rights of Indigenous peoples, including the Mbuti, to their lands, territories and resources.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2024: Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC)
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

facts.text: UNESCO calls for ensuring the involvement of the Indigenous Mbuti and Efe peoples in the management of the Okapi Wildlife Reserve.

nations.name: Karimojong
nations.lands: the Karamoja drylands of north-eastern Uganda

facts.text: The Karimojong, whose economy has long rested on livestock, live mainly in the drylands of north-eastern Uganda, about 1.09 million people in a 2018 estimate.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2024, Uganda chapter (IWGIA yearbook PDF)
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

facts.text: Cultural Heritage Clubs in five secondary schools in Napak and Moroto treat heritage as central to Karimojong history and identity.

source.title: Karamoja Cultural Heritage Education Programme
source.publisher: Kara-Tunga (partner of Cross Cultural Foundation Uganda)

nations.name: !Xun
nations.lands: north-eastern Namibia and southern Angola, and Platfontein near Kimberley in South Africa

facts.text: In South Africa, !Xun and Khwe communities live mainly at Platfontein, near Kimberley.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2024, South Africa chapter (IWGIA yearbook PDF)
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

facts.text: XK FM, a public station first on air in 2000, now broadcasts from Platfontein about 15 hours a day in the !Xun and Khwe languages.

source.title: MEDIA STATEMENT | SABC CELEBRATES THE HISTORY AND CULTURE OF THE !XU AND KHWE

nations.name: Maasai
nations.lands: southern Kenya and northern Tanzania, on both sides of the border

facts.text: In 2025 Tanzania's Simanjiro district paused carbon project signings for 30 days to respond to community concerns, which IWGIA read as a sign that communities are starting to be heard.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2026: Tanzania
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

facts.text: Maasai people speak Maa, a Nilotic language related to Dinka, Kalenjin and Nuer.

nations.name: Korana
nations.lands: Kimberley and the Free State province, South Africa

facts.text: Korana communities live mainly in Kimberley and in the Free State province.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2024, South Africa chapter (IWGIA yearbook PDF)
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

facts.text: In their own !Ora language, the Korana's name for themselves is !Orakua or !Orana.

source.title: Kora: A Lost Khoisan Language of the early Cape and the Gariep, Introduction (Menán du Plessis)

nations.name: Afar
nations.lands: the Afar region of north-eastern Ethiopia, the Dankalia coast of Eritrea, and Djibouti

facts.text: In 2008 Afar pastoralists set up the Afar Pastoralist Council so they could raise their voices at regional, national and international level.

source.title: Afar Pastoralist Council holds Inaugural General Meeting

facts.text: Ethiopia's Afar State is home to about 1.8 million Afar people, by a government projection.

source.title: The Indigenous World 2024, Eritrea chapter (IWGIA yearbook PDF)
source.publisher: IWGIA (International Work Group for Indigenous Affairs)

nations.name: Syilx Okanagan Nation
nations.lands: The Okanagan, Similkameen and Nicola areas of British Columbia, Canada, and northern Washington State, United States

facts.text: Historically the Okanagan Nation Alliance represented eight member communities: seven in Canada and the Colville Confederated Tribes in Washington State.
The Okanagan Nation Alliance reports that the new Okanagan Dam Fish Passage, after years of advocacy and planning, lets salmon reach Okanagan Lake for the first time in nearly 100 years.

nations.name: Kahnawà:ke
nations.lands: On the south shore of the St. Lawrence River, near Montreal, Quebec, Canada

facts.text: For more than a hundred years, many people from Kahnawà:ke, mostly men, have worked in the ironworking trade, much of it in the United States.
About 8,000 people live in Kahnawà:ke, on the banks of the St. Lawrence River about 10 kilometres south of Montreal.

nations.name: Nunavik Inuit
nations.lands: Nunavik, northern Quebec, Canada: 15 villages along Hudson Bay, Hudson Strait and Ungava Bay

facts.text: Makivvik, an Inuktitut name meaning 'to rise up', protects Nunavik Inuit rights under the 1975 James Bay and Northern Quebec Agreement, Canada's first comprehensive Inuit land claim.
Language retention among Nunavik Inuit is over 95 percent, and Inuktitut remains the main language spoken in the region.

nations.name: Inuit of Nunavut
nations.lands: Nunavut, Canada: the Qikiqtaaluk, Kivalliq and Kitikmeot regions

facts.text: Nunavut became Canada's newest territory on April 1, 1999, and Inuktitut is an official language of its government with Inuinnaqtun, English and French.
Under the agreement Inuit own about 350,000 square kilometres of land, including about 35,000 square kilometres with mineral rights.

nations.name: Wolastoqiyik
nations.lands: The Wolastoq (Saint John River) watershed, from the Bay of Fundy to the St. Lawrence: New Brunswick and Quebec in Canada, and Maine in the United States

facts.text: Six Wolastoqey communities in New Brunswick, Matawaskiye, Neqotkuk, Pilick, Sitansisk, Welamukotuk and Wotstak, work together through the Wolastoqey Nation in New Brunswick.
The Wolastoqiyik are the people of the Wolastoq watershed, a homeland of land, sea and fresh water reaching from the Bay of Fundy to the St. Lawrence River.

nations.name: Siksika Nation
nations.lands: East of Calgary, Alberta, Canada; part of the Blackfoot Confederacy

facts.text: Siksika's coat of arms, registered with the Canadian Heraldic Authority in June 1992, was the first registered by any Nation in Canada.
Siksika Nation has about 7,800 members, and its language is Siksika, or Blackfoot.

nations.name: Nuu-chah-nulth
nations.lands: The west coast of Vancouver Island, British Columbia, Canada

facts.text: The Nuu-chah-nulth Tribal Council serves fourteen Nuu-chah-nulth First Nations with about 10,000 members, grouped in three regions.
The Council's vision is self-government that builds strong, healthy Nuu-chah-nulth communities.

nations.name: Inuit
nations.lands: Inuit Nunangat: the Inuvialuit Settlement Region, Nunavut, Nunavik and Nunatsiavut in Arctic Canada

facts.text: Roughly 60 percent of Inuit can hold a conversation in Inuktut, the Inuit language.
Most Inuit in Canada live in 51 communities across Inuit Nunangat, a homeland covering about 40 percent of Canada's land and 72 percent of its coastline.

nations.name: xʷməθkʷəy̓əm
nations.lands: The Fraser River estuary, including much of Metro Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada

facts.text: Musqueam is a strong, growing community of more than 1,300 members, many living on the Musqueam reserve near the mouth of the Fraser River.
The name xʷməθkʷəy̓əm means place of the məθkʷəy̓, a plant, and Musqueam people are traditionally hən̓q̓əmin̓əm̓ speakers.

nations.name: Inuvialuit
nations.lands: The Inuvialuit Settlement Region in the western Arctic, Northwest Territories and Yukon, Canada

facts.text: Six communities lie within the Inuvialuit Settlement Region: Aklavik, Inuvik, Paulatuk, Sachs Harbour, Tuktoyaktuk and Ulukhaktok.
One of the agreement's basic goals is keeping Inuvialuit cultural identity and values strong as northern society changes.

nations.name: Kainai
nations.lands: Southern Alberta, Canada, with its main community at Standoff; part of the Blackfoot Confederacy

facts.text: The Blood Tribe's stated mission is to preserve and protect its lands, culture, language and traditions in the spirit of Kainayssini.
In 2026 the Blood Tribe Land Management Department won a Prairie Conservation Award.

nations.name: Eeyou
also: Grand Council of the Crees (Eeyou Istchee)
nations.lands: Eeyou Istchee, the lands east of James Bay and Hudson Bay in northern Quebec, Canada

facts.text: Each Eeyou First Nation runs its own local government, and every elected Chief also sits on the board of the Grand Council of the Crees to address shared issues.

source.title: The Eeyou of Eeyou Istchee
source.publisher: Grand Council of the Crees (Eeyou Istchee) / Cree Nation Government

facts.text: Eeyou Istchee is home to more than 20,000 people.

source.title: The Eeyou of Eeyou Istchee
source.publisher: Grand Council of the Crees (Eeyou Istchee) / Cree Nation Government

nations.name: Nation Wendat
nations.lands: Wendake, near Québec City, within the traditional territory Onyionhwentsïio’ in Quebec, Canada

facts.text: After the Wendat language went dormant in the 1800s, the Yawenda project (2007 to 2012) brought language specialists and community members together to revive it.
The Nation counts more than 300 Wendat businesses, including many artisans, artists and cultural organizations.

nations.name: səlilwətaɬ
nations.lands: Burrard Inlet (səlilwət) in North Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada

facts.text: Tsleil-Waututh people see caring for the lands and waters of their territory as a birthright and obligation, so future generations can thrive.
Tsleil-Waututh means 'People of the Inlet'. The Nation's language is hən̓q̓əmin̓əm, in which its name is səlilwətaɬ.

nations.name: Akwesasne
nations.lands: Along the St. Lawrence River where Ontario, Quebec and New York State meet, in Canada and the United States

facts.text: Akwesasne spans lands in Quebec, Ontario and New York State, and three separate but linked political bodies govern it.
Kanien'kéha, the Mohawk language, remains central to identity in Akwesasne and is actively taught in its schools.

nations.name: Sḵwx̱wú7mesh Úxwumixw
nations.lands: The North Shore of Vancouver and the Squamish River valley, British Columbia, Canada

facts.text: The Nation's roots lie in several communities that became one government in 1923. Most members live on Vancouver's North Shore, others along the Squamish River.
The Squamish language is a sign of resilience: dozens of Nation members are learning it from their Elders as a second language.

nations.name: Haida Nation
nations.lands: Haida Gwaii, an archipelago off the north coast of British Columbia, Canada

facts.text: The Council of the Haida Nation works to steward the lands and waters of Haida territories and carry Haida culture and language to future generations.
In April 2024 British Columbia and the Council of the Haida Nation signed the Rising Tide agreement, a first of its kind recognizing Haida Aboriginal title in Haida Gwaii.

source.title: For Immediate Release: Haida Nation, B.C. recognize Haida Aboriginal title, a historic first in Canada

nations.name: Mescalero Apache
nations.lands: South-central New Mexico, US (Mescalero Apache Reservation)

facts.text: Today three peoples, the Mescalero, Lipan and Chiricahua Apache, together make up the Mescalero Apache Tribe on a 463,000 acre reservation.
The Mescalero Apache Tribe owns and runs the Inn of the Mountain Gods Resort and the Ski Apache ski area.

source.title: Official Website of the Mescalero Apache Tribe

nations.name: Jicarilla Apache
nations.lands: North-central New Mexico, US, along the Colorado line and across the Continental Divide (Dulce)

facts.text: The Jicarilla Apache Nation reservation spans more than 879,917 acres in north-central New Mexico, and Dulce is its only community and tribal headquarters.
After 1887 the Jicarilla moved their individual allotments back into tribal ownership, keeping their lands and water rights together.

nations.name: Akimel O’otham
nations.lands: Gila River Indian Community, south of Phoenix, Arizona, US, shared with the Pee Posh (Maricopa)

facts.text: The Akimel O’otham welcomed the Pee Posh (Maricopa) to the Gila River long ago, and the two peoples still share its lands and resources today.
Akimel O’otham basket weaving is in revival, and in 2004 the community dedicated the Huhugam Heritage Center to care for its heritage.

nations.name: Yoreme
nations.lands: Southern Sonora (Etchojoa, Huatabampo, Navojoa) and northern Sinaloa (Ahome, El Fuerte, Guasave), Mexico

facts.text: Yoreme communities have traditional governors. In December 2025 they met Mexico’s federal agrarian office to set a path for continuing the Yoreme-Mayo Justice Plan.

source.title: Atienden Plan de Justicia al pueblo Yoreme-Mayo de Sonora

facts.text: Yoreme patron saint fiestas strengthen the social networks that link communities across Mayo lands and keep Yoreme identity alive.

source.title: Mayos
source.publisher: Sistema de Información Cultural, Secretaría de Cultura (Mexico)

nations.name: Ute Mountain Ute Tribe
nations.lands: Towaoc and reservation lands in southwestern Colorado and northwestern New Mexico; White Mesa, Utah, United States

facts.text: The Ute Mountain Ute Tribe identifies itself as the Weenuche band of the Ute Nation, with its tribal offices in Towaoc, Colorado.
White Mesa Administration supports community members with employment, education and access to basic services in White Mesa, Utah.

nations.name: Comcaac
nations.lands: Desert coast of Sonora on the Gulf of California, Mexico, including Punta Chueca, El Desemboque and Tiburón Island

facts.text: In 1975 Mexico declared the Canal del Infiernillo an exclusive Comcaac fishing zone and symbolically granted them Tiburón Island, a nature reserve, as communal land.

source.title: Seris
source.publisher: Sistema de Información Cultural, Secretaría de Cultura (Mexico)

facts.text: Comcaac artisans weave coritas, baskets made since before Spanish contact. A very large one can take a year or two to finish.

source.title: Seris
source.publisher: Sistema de Información Cultural, Secretaría de Cultura (Mexico)

nations.name: Hualapai
nations.lands: Northwestern Arizona, US, along the Grand Canyon and Colorado River (Peach Springs)

facts.text: The name Hualapai means People of the Tall Pines.
The Hualapai Reservation, set up in 1883, covers about one million acres along 108 miles of the Grand Canyon and Colorado River.

nations.name: Warihó and Macurawe
nations.lands: Foothills of the Sierra Madre Occidental on the Chihuahua and Sonora border, Mexico

facts.text: The people call themselves Macurawe in Sonora and Warihó in Chihuahua. Their Uto-Aztecan language has two variants and bridges Tarahumara and Mayo.

source.title: Guarijíos
source.publisher: Sistema de Información Cultural, Secretaría de Cultura (Mexico)

facts.text: Warihó and Macurawe families weave baskets, mats and hats from palm and fiber and build harps, violins and guitars. Their craft work is family based and rests with women.

source.title: Guarijíos
source.publisher: Sistema de Información Cultural, Secretaría de Cultura (Mexico)

nations.name: Diné
nations.lands: Diné Bikéyah (Navajoland) across Arizona, New Mexico and Utah, US

facts.text: The Navajo Nation Council, the Nation’s governing body, has 24 delegates elected from legislative districts.
Diné Bikéyah, the Navajo Nation, covers more than 27,000 square miles across Arizona, New Mexico and Utah, larger than 10 of the 50 US states.

nations.name: Havasu Baaja
nations.lands: Havasu Canyon in the Grand Canyon, Arizona, US (village of Supai)

facts.text: Supai is so remote that the US Postal Service carries all mail in and out of the canyon by mule train.
The Havasupai reservation was set up in 1880 and greatly enlarged in 1975. It covers 188,077 acres beside the South Rim of the Grand Canyon.

nations.name: White Mountain Apache
nations.lands: White Mountains of east-central Arizona, US (Fort Apache Indian Reservation, Whiteriver)

facts.text: The White Mountain Apache own and run Sunrise, one of the largest ski resorts in the Southwest, and rare Apache trout swim in reservation streams.
White Mountain Apache people live on 1.6 million acres of their ancestral homeland, the Fort Apache Indian Reservation, set aside in 1891.

nations.name: Tonto Apache Tribe
nations.lands: Payson, Gila County, Arizona, United States

facts.text: The Tonto Apache Tribe is based beside Payson in northwestern Gila County, Arizona.
In 2010, land for the Tonto Apache Tribe was acquired in trust following a land exchange with the U.S. Forest Service.

source.title: Reservation proclamation for trust land belonging to the Tonto Apache Tribe of Arizona

nations.name: Yavapai
nations.lands: Central and western Arizona, US, including Fort McDowell near Phoenix and Prescott

facts.text: In September 2026 the Fort McDowell Yavapai Nation, about 950 members, marked 123 years since its land was set aside in 1903.

source.title: Welcome to Fort McDowell Yavapai Nation

facts.text: In 1976 Fort McDowell Yavapai community members voted 144 to 57 against selling their land for the Orme Dam, and in 1981 the dam was called off.

nations.name: Ohkay Owingeh
nations.lands: Where the Rio Grande and Rio Chama meet, northern New Mexico, US

facts.text: Ohkay Owingeh is the headquarters of the Eight Northern Pueblo Tribal Council.
The people have long called their home Ohkay Owingeh, place of the strong people in Tewa, and officially restored that name in place of San Juan, given in 1598.

nations.name: Cocopah
nations.lands: Lower Colorado River and delta: south of Yuma and near Somerton, Arizona, US, and the Mexicali valley of Baja California and San Luis Río Colorado, Sonora, Mexico

facts.text: About 1,000 Cocopah tribal members live and work on or near their reservation south of Yuma, Arizona, which was established in 1917.
Since 2003 the Cucapá of El Mayor, Baja California, and the Cocopah of Somerton, Arizona, have met each year with dances, songs, crafts and food.

source.title: Cucapás
source.publisher: Sistema de Información Cultural, Secretaría de Cultura (Mexico)

nations.name: Nuche
nations.lands: Southwestern Colorado (Ignacio, Towaoc), northeastern Utah (Uintah and Ouray) and nearby New Mexico and Utah lands, US

facts.text: There are three Ute tribes today: the Southern Ute (Mouache and Capote bands), the Ute Mountain Ute (Weenuche band) and the Northern Ute in Utah.
The Ute Mountain Ute Tribe teaches the Ute language to Head Start children ages 2 to 5 and holds evening language classes for adults.

nations.name: Confederated Tribes of Siletz Indians
nations.lands: Siletz, on the central Oregon coast; ancestral territory across western Oregon into southwest Washington and northern California

facts.text: After lobbying Congress, the Confederated Tribes of Siletz Indians won repeal of federal termination in 1977.
The Tribe's Athabaskan language dictionary, Nuu-wee-ya' (Our words), holds about 12,000 entries, and a Talking Dictionary lets learners hear words spoken aloud.

source.title: Language - Confederated Tribes of Siletz Indians

nations.name: Puyallup Tribe of Indians
nations.lands: Shores of southern Puget Sound and the Puyallup River, Tacoma area, Washington

facts.text: One of the most urban tribes in the United States, the Puyallup still fish, hunt and travel the waters of the Puyallup River.
The Tribe gives its name as puyaləpabš, meaning people at the bend at the bottom of the river.

nations.name: Morongo Band of Mission Indians
nations.lands: Morongo Indian Reservation beneath the San Gorgonio Mountains, Riverside County, California

facts.text: Morongo tribal members elect a seven-member Tribal Council to lead their independent tribal government.
Established in 1865, the Morongo Indian Reservation now spans more than 35,000 acres.

nations.name: Federated Indians of Graton Rancheria
nations.lands: Sonoma and Marin counties, California, with a reservation near Rohnert Park

facts.text: Graton Rancheria launched its own Tribal TANF program serving low-income Native American families in Sonoma and Marin counties.
Graton Rancheria, a federation of Coast Miwok and Southern Pomo groups, regained federal recognition through a law signed on December 27, 2000.

nations.name: Yurok Tribe
nations.lands: Lower Klamath River and the Pacific coast of far northern California, United States

facts.text: When Yurok people speak of themselves, they say Oohl, which means Indian people.
On June 30, 2026, Save the Redwoods League conveyed 125 acres on Prairie Creek, in the heart of Yurok ancestral territory, back to the Yurok Tribe.

nations.name: Viejas Band of Kumeyaay Indians
nations.lands: Viejas Reservation in the mountains east of San Diego, California; the wider Kumeyaay homeland reaches into Baja California, Mexico

facts.text: Viejas extends its community work beyond San Diego to Kumeyaay relatives in Baja California, Mexico.
Viejas government rests on participatory democracy, with tribal officials elected by the general council to four-year terms.

nations.name: Pyramid Lake Paiute Tribe
nations.lands: Pyramid Lake and its reservation, about 35 miles northeast of Reno, Nevada

facts.text: The Tribe's Language Program offers community Paiute classes, lessons inside schools and meetings with fluent speakers.
The reservation covers 475,000 acres around Pyramid Lake, which runs about 27 miles long and 11 miles wide.

nations.name: Confederated Tribes of Grand Ronde
nations.lands: Grand Ronde, Yamhill County, northwestern Oregon; ancestral ties across western Oregon, northern California and southwest Washington

facts.text: A nine-member Tribal Council, elected by voting members, governs about 5,400 enrolled members of a confederation of over 30 tribes and bands.
Once at risk of disappearing, Chinuk Wawa is growing again and is actively taught and used in Grand Ronde cultural education.

source.title: Chinuk Wawa Language | Confederated Tribes of Grand Ronde

nations.name: Nimiipuu
nations.lands: North-central Idaho, with homelands across present-day Idaho, Washington, Oregon and Montana

facts.text: Nimipuutímt, the Nez Perce language, is a core part of Nimiipuu culture.
Headquartered in Lapwai, Idaho, the Nez Perce Reservation spans about 770,000 acres.

nations.name: Lummi Nation
nations.lands: Northernmost coast of Washington State and the waters of Puget Sound, with ancestral lands reaching into southern British Columbia

facts.text: Northwest Indian College, with its main campus on the Lummi Reservation, is the only accredited tribal college serving Washington, Oregon and Idaho.

source.title: About | Northwest Indian College | Accredited Tribal College

facts.text: The Lhaq'temish, the Lummi People, describe themselves as fishers, hunters, gatherers and harvesters of the Puget Sound shores and waters.

nations.name: Karuk Tribe
nations.lands: Klamath River country of northern California, with tribal offices in Happy Camp

facts.text: The Karuk Language Program teaches all ages through community classes, school partnerships and immersion, linking learners with fluent speakers.
The Karuk People's Center in Happy Camp opened in September 2002 and holds a museum, library, basketweaving classroom and the language program office.

nations.name: Hoopa Valley Tribe
nations.lands: Hoopa Valley along the Trinity River, Humboldt County, northern California

facts.text: The Hoopa Valley Tribe runs its own Fisheries Department, which counts the harvest and spawning returns of salmon, steelhead, sturgeon and lamprey.
Tribal fisheries crews made major progress restoring the lower reaches of Supply Creek and Mill Creek between 2015 and 2018.

nations.name: Quinault Indian Nation
nations.lands: Southwestern corner of Washington's Olympic Peninsula, between the Olympic Mountains and the Pacific Ocean

facts.text: The Nation has a Taholah Village Relocation Master Plan that includes planning for an upper village, and its Planning Department is updating the plan for 2026.

source.title: Taholah Village Relocation | Quinault Indian Nation, WA

facts.text: The Quinault Language Department works to revitalize the Quinault language, with in-person classes in Taholah, Queets and Hoquiam.

source.title: Language Department | Quinault Indian Nation, WA

nations.name: Tuolumne Band of Me-Wuk Indians
nations.lands: Sierra Nevada foothills, Tuolumne County, California

facts.text: In January 2005 the Tribe opened the Tuolumne Me-Wuk Indian Health Center.

source.title: History - The Tuolumne Band of Me-Wuk Indians

facts.text: Tuolumne Rancheria began in 1910 with 289.52 acres; today the Tribe holds more than 1,700 acres of fee and trust land.

source.title: History - The Tuolumne Band of Me-Wuk Indians

nations.name: Swinomish Indian Tribal Community
nations.lands: Swinomish Reservation near La Conner, Skagit County, Washington

facts.text: The Swinomish Tribe monitors air quality in partnership with the EPA, with two major oil refineries right next to its reservation.
Swinomish monitors record real-time data on particulates, ozone and nitrogen dioxide, plus weather such as wind, temperature, humidity and precipitation.

nations.name: Baniwa
nations.lands: Içana river and the Upper Rio Negro in Amazonas, Brazil, and neighboring Colombia and Venezuela

facts.text: The Baniwa speak languages of the Arawak family along the Içana river.
Baniwa communities live where Brazil meets Colombia and Venezuela, along the Içana river in the Upper Rio Negro region.

nations.name: Wapichana
nations.lands: Northeastern Roraima, Brazil, and the South Rupununi in southwestern Guyana

facts.text: In 2012 Wapichan leaders in Guyana presented a community map and land plan titled Thinking Together for those Coming Behind Us.

source.title: Wapichan people in Guyana present territorial map and community proposals to save ancestral forests

facts.text: The Wapichana language is classified in the Arawak language family.

nations.name: Guarani Mbya
nations.lands: Villages across southern and southeastern Brazil, eastern Paraguay, Misiones province in Argentina, and near Montevideo in Uruguay

facts.text: The Comissão Guarani Yvyrupa, founded in 2006, brings together Guarani collectives in six states of southern and southeastern Brazil.
In Guarani, yvyrupa names the structure that holds up the land, recalling free movement across territory before today's borders.

nations.name: Sápara
nations.lands: Rainforest of Pastaza province in the Ecuadorian Amazon, straddling the border with Peru

facts.text: The Sápara live in a part of the Amazon rainforest that straddles Ecuador and Peru.

source.title: Oral heritage and cultural manifestations of the Zápara people

facts.text: Sápara knowledge of the forest shows in their rich vocabulary for plants and animals and in their knowledge of the forest's medicinal plants.
